name: starter-kit
prompt:
Add a starter kit. When a player joins, the server gives them a starting count of each block type, stored as number attributes on the Player (for example Brick = 20).

Designers want to tune the counts in Studio's Properties window, so keep them as attributes on a Configuration instance named StarterKit somewhere under ReplicatedStorage: Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10.

On the client, once the player's counts are set, show a one-time Roblox notification (StarterGui:SetCore("SendNotification", ...)) listing what they got. The block types are in src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/BlockTypes.luau.

checks.text: The built place has one Configuration named StarterKit under ReplicatedStorage with the five counts as number attributes
A Script under ServerScriptService reads StarterKit and a LocalScript where LocalScripts run calls SendNotification

rubric: StarterKit is declared in files Rojo maps into the place: a .model.json with className Configuration and attributes, or a folder whose init.meta.json sets them, at a path the project mounts under ReplicatedStorage (such as src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json) or through a node added to default.project.json. A file directly in src/ReplicatedStorage isn't part of the place and fails this.
The five counts are JSON numbers (Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10), not strings.

The server part is a .server.luau file under src/ServerScriptService (a Script), and the client part is a .client.luau file under src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts or another folder where LocalScripts run (such as StarterGui). Shared code, if any, is a plain .luau module under src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared.

The code reads StarterKit at the DataModel path the files actually produce (for example ReplicatedStorage.Shared.StarterKit, with WaitForChild on the client) and sets a count for every type in BlockTypes.List, treating a missing attribute as 0 or reporting it.

The server also handles players who joined before it connected (Players:GetPlayers()). The client shows the notification once, after the counts exist, and guards SetCore, which errors until the core scripts register it (for example pcall with a few retries).
No unrelated changes, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua pass. If default.project.json is edited, it stays valid and changes only what the kit needs.
judge_facts: Rojo 7.7.1 (built in the sandbox and read back with Lune): StarterKit.model.json containing { "className": "Configuration", "attributes": { "Brick": 20, "Window": 0 } } builds a Configuration named StarterKit with number attributes Brick = 20 and Window = 0, and a folder whose init.meta.json sets className Configuration and attributes builds the same kind of instance.

In this project, files directly in src/ReplicatedStorage (outside src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared) are not part of the place: the ReplicatedStorage node in default.project.json has no $path, only the children Shared ($path src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared) and Packages ($path roblox_packages). Verified with rojo sourcemap, Rojo 7.7.1.

This project's README.md (and Rojo 7.7.1's sourcemap output): Name.server.luau becomes a Script, Name.client.luau a LocalScript, and any other Name.luau a ModuleScript; Foo.spec.luau becomes the ModuleScript Foo.spec.
notes: New-files branch: script suffixes, which folders are mounted, and declaring a non-script instance (Configuration with attributes) in files. The trap is src/ReplicatedStorage/StarterKit.model.json, which isn't mapped because the ReplicatedStorage node has no $path. The checks read the built tree from rojo sourcemap, so they accept any correct location.
